operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case (Film_ID, Rank_in_series, Openning_year) and must be double-quoted; column lookup case-insensitive.
Tiny tables: film=5, cinema=10, schedule=7 rows; original_values are complete, no rowid sampling needed.
schedule has composite PK (Cinema_ID, Film_ID) -> composite-PK members get max_l0=30 in TS; PK-duplicate row dropping applies to the tuple.
schedule.Film_ID and schedule.Cinema_ID are both PK members AND FK children; FK fill draws from parent's final filtered column.
All columns notnull=0 despite being PKs; sqlite PK on non-INT columns would be NOT NULL but here PKs are INT so no implicit constraint issue.
schedule.Date is TEXT storing '21 May','11 July','2 Aug' — no year, no zero-padded day; Date fuzzer will NOT dispatch (declared TEXT -> String).
film.Original_air_date TEXT stores 'September 21–25, 1992' with en-dash ranges — String fuzzer, not Date.
film.Production_code TEXT stores '50021–50025' with en-dash — String fuzzer; int-like prefix but not pure int.
cinema.Openning_year INT (misspelled) holds 2009-2015; Number fuzzer with scale from INT (no args) -> range [-10,10] roughly, will NOT produce plausible years.
schedule.Price declared 'float' (lowercase) -> Number family, scale from no args; storage real; samples 8.99-15.99.
Directed_by has non-ASCII 'Treviño' — String fuzzer CHARSET is ASCII-only, so accented chars never regenerated.
No dangling FKs, no self-references, no views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs.
operator_ts_expectations: film.Film_ID, cinema.Cinema_ID: Number fuzzer, single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, fresh draws perturbed by +-1/+-2; values stay near [-10,10] plus pool literals.
schedule FK columns draw from parent's final Film_ID/Cinema_ID lists with replacement -> ties/duplicates in schedule expected, PK dedup then drops rows.

schedule.Date, film.Original_air_date, film.Production_code, cinema.Name, film.Title, film.Directed_by: String fuzzer, random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, 50% contaminated -> implausible values (FN risk for LIKE/date-format predicates).
cinema.Openning_year, film.Rank_in_series, film.Number_in_season, schedule.Show_times_per_day: Number fuzzer small range -> implausible (years, ranks) -> FN on range predicates.
schedule.Price: Number float, range ~[-10,10] with +-0.01/0.02 perturbation -> misses 8.99-15.99 band -> FN on price thresholds.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like elements and %-stripped variants -> some plausible numeric strings survive.
Date fuzzer never fires (no 'date'/'timestamp' in declared types) -> text dates are random strings, so date-format queries (strftime, month names) get FP/FN.
Tiny original sizes (5-10) mean original_values contribute only 5 sampled elements per column; pool literals dominate.
Composite PK on schedule: TS drops duplicate (Cinema_ID,Film_ID) tuples, so join cardinalities stay small; missing ties -> FP on COUNT/aggregate queries.

FK consistency: schedule rows always reference existing cinema/film after parent filtering, so join queries return rows; but parent PK dedup may shrink parents below child demand -> NULLs possible if parent empties (unlikely here).
Number fuzzer list_max quirk (overwrites with full-range max) means pool literals like 2010 do not widen the range -> years stay small.
String fuzzer contaminate 50% -> many garbage strings; equality predicates on Title/Name rarely match -> FN.
